claims.text: The starting alloy is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% each of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a disordered, single-phase FCC solid solution.
This starting alloy has favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and compressive strength.
The relatively low hardness and strength are governed by the absence of nanoscale Ti-rich chemically ordered regions.
Nanoscale Ti-rich chemically ordered regions would impede dislocation motion.
In the absence of these regions, dislocations move relatively easily, producing low hardening while retaining ductility.
Sub-solidus annealing at about 500 °C for controlled durations can induce nanoscale Ti-rich local chemical ordering.
Such annealing can produce the proposed ordering without developing extensive intermetallic phases.
Post-treatments including annealing can enhance the mechanical performance of high-entropy alloys.
Annealing promotes local chemical ordering into nanoscale Ti-rich clusters in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The Ti-rich clusters pin dislocations.
Cluster-mediated dislocation pinning increases hardness and compressive strength.
Cluster-mediated strengthening reduces ductility relative to the as-cast state.
Annealed samples will have higher hardness and compressive strength than the as-cast control.
Annealed samples will show a moderate reduction in plasticity relative to the as-cast control.
TEM/EDS will reveal nanoscale Ti-rich regions after annealing.
CoCrFeNiTix alloys can transform from a simple FCC structure to sigma, R, or Laves intermetallic phases as Ti concentration varies.
Annealing outside 400–600 °C may cause full intermetallic-phase formation and brittle behavior.
The proposed comparison uses as-cast controls and samples annealed at 500 °C for 1, 5, and 10 hours, followed by hardness, compression, TEM/EDS, and XRD measurements from room temperature to 600 °C.
Failure to observe both Ti-rich ordering and increased hardness and compressive strength, or observation of intermetallic-driven brittle failure, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
